newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end at third record in a row.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end at third record in a row.

text.p: Swiss shares closed at a third straight record high in both the blue-chip and broad indexes on Friday as gains in several high-profile stocks propelled the market.

"We are watching the situation with disbelief," one trader commented on nearly one percent index gains after Thursday's jump of two percent. Volume was described as above average amid derivatives-linked demand and foreign buying.
"The environment remains brilliant, but, of course, a lot of people get the jitters given such levels," one trader said.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) ended 51.5 points or 0.93 percent higher at 5,561.8 points.
The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) added 28.68 points or 0.82 percent to 3,518.12.
Bourse volume was at 2.93 billion Swiss francs. The expiry of options and futures index contracts was smooth.
Roche certificates took the lead among major pharmaceuticals, adding 275 francs to 13,245.

Dealers said Roche profited from a positive analyst report and from news that a study showed a combination of three drugs including its Invirase reduced the onset of AIDS much better than two-drug treatment.
One trader said the stock also had renewed potential after Novartis's recent strong gains.
Novartis registereds, which jumped four percent on Thursday, slowed their upward drive. The stock ended 15 francs higher at 2,290.
Banks temporarily fell from grace, one trader said. UBS bearers, which on Thursday were among the day's winners, slid five francs to 1,719. Credit Suisse and SBC also lost ground.
Swiss Re stood out among blue-chips, surging 82 francs, or 4.13 francs, to 2,067. A dealer said Swiss Re had broken resistance at 2,005/2,010 and now had a potential to move to 2,100/2,150 francs.
